p. 30 VIIa Atr, below, p. 262.

p. 31 Aelfric's Pastorale14; p. 40 Polity 23. 22. 2515;

continuing in the same hand (pp. 33—64 originally formed a single quire), probably from dg,

p. 43 Northu, below, p. 380; p. 46 II. III Eg, below, p. 194; p. 48 V Atr, below, p. 236; continuing in the same hand p. 51 Polity 2416; p. 52 homily17.

p. 53 I As, below, p. 146; continuing in the same hand, homilies18; p. 57 Polity 25, pieces19; p. 61 homilies20. —

p. 87 VIII Atr 36, below, p. 267; Polity 2—4. 6. 11. 19 beginning. 23 beginning. 13. 14 beginning. 15 beginning. 16. 22. 17. 25. 24. In the same hand:

p. 93 VIII Atr, below, p. 263; p. 96 I As rubric only, below, p. 146; p. 96 I Em, below, p. 184.

p. 97 Canones Eadgari1; in the same hand p. 101 f., from doi Geþyncðo; Norðleoð; Mirce; Að; Had, below, pp. 456—464; in the same hand p. 103 homily2; p. 108 De ecclesiasticis gradibus3; pp. 112—15 Benediktiner-Offiz.4; p. 114 De confessione5; p. 125 Theodori De aegris6.

p. 126 I. II Cnut in fragments, with additions, below, p. 278; p. 128 VI Atr 16—49, below, p. 252.; in the same hand:

p. 130 Polity 19 with an addition; p. 131 Apollonius of Tyre7; p. 145 the rest, and 146 blank: end of a quire.

pp. 147—51 The Saints in England8.

p. 151 another hand. From Aelfric's Genesis c. 379.

p. 161 same hand as p. 1: Be domes dæge10; Lar, Oratio poetica; p. 167 another hand: Lord's prayer, Doxology11; p. 170 another hand: De confessione12; p. 177 f. blank, then another quire, another hand: p. 179 Theodulf's Canones, the original of the Ecclesiast. institutes13; pp. 222—31 = Eccles. inst.14; p. 274, beginning of 12th century, Usuard15.

D was copied by the Liber Oxon. Cradok, and that by Vs.

wormald.shelfmark: Cambridge, Corpus Christi College, MS 201 (pp. 1–178; Parker's added Exeter section from CCCC 191 at the end)
wormald.wormald_date: s. xi^med (Table 4.1, p. 164); Ker dates pp. 1–7, 161–7 (scribe 1) s. xiⁱⁿ and pp. 8–160, 167–76 s. xi^med (p. 206 n. 165); scribes 2–4 work about half a century after scribe 1 and look contemporary with each other (pp. 206, 209)
wormald.wormald_origin: Winchester, New Minster (Table 4.1, p. 164): scribe 4's hand recurs in a New Minster MS; the Regularis Concordia has a typically Winchester liturgical feature; the Resting-places text is close to the New Minster Liber Vitae (p. 209). Section b) copies a Wulfstan pastoral manual with additions made at York (Northu, probably by a York archbishop or his staff after 1023), perhaps sent to Winchester by Ælfric Puttoc, archbishop of York, said to have been prior of Winchester (pp. 208–10). The only one of the twenty manuscripts surveyed not from a cathedral (p. 263). Archbishop Parker erased the first 38 lines of p. 1, added a contents-list and bound in an unrelated Exeter copy of Theodulf's Capitulary (Latin and OE) from CCCC 191 (p. 206 and n. 167).
wormald.laws: All in section b) (scribe 2, pp. 8–145): VIIa Atr (= Hom.N 39) with its variant Hom.N 35 (two versions of the 1009 edict); Northu; II–III Eg; V Atr; I As; VIII Atr (complete text of the 1014 code); I Em; Geþyncðo, Norðleod, Mirce, Að (titled 'Be Mirciscan aðe/Mercena lage', p. 248 n. 332), Had (status tracts assembled and rewritten by Wulfstan); Cn 1018 (Wulfstan's 'framework document' for the 1018 Anglo-Danish agreement) (Table 4.3, pp. 204–5; pp. 208 and n. 178; 248 n. 332). Also Wulfstan's 'Canons of Edgar' (Can. Eg.).
wormald.laws_liebermann: VII a Atr, Northu, II Eg, III Eg, V Atr, I As, VIII Atr, I Em, Geþyncðo, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, I Cn, II Cn, VI Atr
wormald.other_contents: Seven sections by four scribes (Table 4.3, pp. 204–5): a) OE Regularis Concordia fragment (scribe 1, unfinished, start lost); b) about three-quarters of Wulfstan's genuine homilies plus others, the complete first edition of the Institutes of Polity and materials for the second, Ælfric's Pastoral Letter II, Benedictine Office, confessional texts, the laws, and the OE Apollonius of Tyre; c) Saints' Resting-places (Halgan, Secgan); d) OE Genesis 37:1–47:18 (Joseph story, scribe 3); e) OE Judgement Day and other verse (scribe 1); f) OE Lord's Prayer and Gloria (scribe 2); g) Latin forms of confession and absolution, incl. for women (scribe 4). Parker added Theodulf's Capitulary from Exeter at the end.
wormald.overview: Corpus 201 is a tall, narrow mid-eleventh-century MS, most probably assembled at the New Minster, Winchester, by several scribes who built on an unfinished collection of devotional texts begun half a century earlier. Its core (section b) copies a Wulfstan manual of Christian instruction, fuller than Nero A.i(B): homilies, the Institutes of Polity, the Canons of Edgar and an even larger group of Wulfstan's legal texts — VIIa and VIII Æthelred, V Æthelred, I Æthelstan, I Edmund, II–III Edgar, the status tracts (Geþyncðo to Had), the Northumbrian Priests' Law and the 1018 Cnut text. That collection seems to have been shaped at York, where the Northumbrian Priests' Law was added, before reaching Winchester, where the MS may have served to train future monk-bishops in both pastoral and governmental duties.
wormald.liebermann_superseded: Liebermann placed the manuscript at Worcester or a dependent house, c. 1050–80; Wormald assigns it to the New Minster, Winchester, s. xi^med (with scribe 1's work s. xiⁱⁿ), and argues that its Wulfstan core reached there by way of York (pp. 208–10; Table 4.1, p. 164).
wormald.key_quote: section b) of Corpus 201 is a manual for the drilling of a Christian society like Nero A.i(B), only fuller (p. 208)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: origin should be New Minster, Winchester (Wormald), not Worcester; date s. xi^med (scribe 1 s. xiⁱⁿ), not c. 1050–80. GUIDE: Liebermann's list includes 'fragments of I–II Cnut with additions' and 'VI Atr 16–49'; Wormald's Table 4.3 and Table 4.1 have neither, but list Cn 1018 (Wulfstan's draft for the 1018 agreement) — presumably what Liebermann treated as I–II Cn fragments; VI Atr is not mentioned by Wormald for this MS in these pages (needs checking in ch. 3 pp. 131–3 / ch. 5). Liebermann's 'p. 274 early 12th century' presumably refers to the Exeter material Parker added from CCCC 191 (Wormald p. 206 n. 167), not to the original book — unverified. Wormald calls 'VIIa Atr' and Hom.N 35 'two variants of the 1009 edict'. Homily editors' siglum is 'C'; Ker no. 49. Dates checked in image: Table 4.1 ‘s. xi^med’; Ker’s ‘s xiⁱⁿ’ / ‘s xi^med’ (p. 206 n. 165); n. 178 reads ‘VIIa Atr (= Hom.N 39) with Hom.N 35’. Table 4.3 (image) confirms the law list.
verify_notes: Checked pp. 197–8, 204–10 (Table 4.3, image), 211 n. 194, 222–3, 248 n. 332, 263 and Table 4.1 (image).
overview: ‘largest group … anywhere’ reduced to Wormald’s ‘even fuller’ than Nero; Apollonius no longer said to have been added at York (Wormald, p. 209, leaves its point of addition open).
origin: p. 263 point corrected — CCCC 201 is the only one of all twenty books not from a cathedral, not ‘of the class’.
liebermann_superseded: ‘shows’ softened to ‘argues’ for the York route.

Corpus 201 is a tall, narrow mid-eleventh-century MS, most probably assembled at the New Minster, Winchester, by several scribes who built on an unfinished collection of devotional texts begun half a century earlier. Its core (section b) copies a Wulfstan manual of Christian instruction, fuller than Nero A.i(B): homilies, the Institutes of Polity, the Canons of Edgar and an even larger group of Wulfstan's legal texts — VIIa and VIII Æthelred, V Æthelred, I Æthelstan, I Edmund, II–III Edgar, the status tracts (Geþyncðo to Had), the Northumbrian Priests' Law and the 1018 Cnut text. That collection seems to have been shaped at York, where the Northumbrian Priests' Law was added, before reaching Winchester, where the MS may have served to train future monk-bishops in both pastoral and governmental duties.

Liebermann placed the manuscript at Worcester or a dependent house, c. 1050–80; Wormald assigns it to the New Minster, Winchester, s. xi^med (with scribe 1's work s. xiⁱⁿ), and argues that its Wulfstan core reached there by way of York (pp. 208–10; Table 4.1, p. 164).
